phases.name: Line control
gateStatements: My lines land roughly where I aimed about 7 times in 10.
My ellipses are smooth and closed, even when they're the wrong shape.
I can draw a box that reads as a box in space without thinking hard.
I've done at least 4 weekend contour sessions.

phases.name: Observation
gateStatements: I can block in overall proportions in the first 90 seconds and not need to shift them.
When I compare a drawing to its reference, my errors are small and scattered rather than the same distortion every time.
I've done at least 4 complexity studies of 25 minutes or longer.

steps.name: Straight lines, dot to dot, 20 reps
instructions: Draw straight lines from dot to dot, 20 reps.
Look at the endpoint, not the pen tip.
steps.commonFailure: Hooking the line at the far end because your eye followed the tip.

subject.text: A blank page. The marks are the subject.

steps.name: Superimposed lines — one line, trace it 5 times without drifting
instructions: Draw one line.
Trace it 5 times without drifting.
steps.commonFailure: Fraying at the far end. The start is always tighter than the finish.

subject.text: A blank page. The marks are the subject.

steps.name: Ghosted lines — hover the motion twice, commit once
instructions: Hover the motion twice without touching the page, then commit once.
15 lines.

subject.text: A blank page. The marks are the subject.

steps.name: Long single-stroke curves, 15 reps
instructions: Draw long curves, one stroke each, 15 reps.

subject.text: A blank page. The marks are the subject.

steps.name: Ellipses in a shallow angled box, fill the row
instructions: Draw a shallow angled box.
Fill the row with ellipses.

subject.text: A blank page. The marks are the subject.

steps.name: Ellipses in a steep box, fill the row
instructions: Draw a steep box.
Fill the row with ellipses.

subject.text: A blank page. The marks are the subject.

steps.name: Ellipse funnel — a curved corridor, ellipses filling it
instructions: Draw a curved corridor.
Fill it with ellipses, all minor axes aligned to the centre line.

subject.text: A blank page. The marks are the subject.

steps.name: Eight freehand boxes, rotated at random
instructions: Draw eight freehand boxes, each rotated at random.

subject.text: A blank page. The marks are the subject.

steps.name: Six boxes with every edge drawn twice
instructions: Draw six boxes.
Draw every edge twice.

subject.text: A blank page. The marks are the subject.

steps.name: Six boxes, each larger than the last
instructions: Draw six boxes, each larger than the last.
The largest fills the page.

subject.text: A blank page. The marks are the subject.

steps.name: Contour studies of 5-10 household objects
instructions: Draw 5-10 household objects, one after another.
One continuous line, no lifting, no erasing.

subject.text: Five to ten household objects — a crumpled receipt, open scissors, keys on a ring, a tangled charging cable.

steps.name: One blind contour
instructions: Eyes on the object only, never on the page.
It will look terrible. That is the drill working.

subject.text: One household object — a wire whisk, a sneaker with loose laces, an adjustable wrench.

steps.name: One object, its 5-8 major angles only
instructions: Draw the 5-8 major angles as straight lines.
Nothing else.

subject.text: The nearest chair, standing and looking down at it.

steps.name: Major angles, measured before committing
instructions: Draw the major angles as straight lines, as before.
Hold your pencil up to compare each real angle before committing.
steps.commonFailure: You will flatten the extremes. Steep angles get drawn shallower than they are.

subject.text: Your own shoe from behind, laces toward you.

steps.name: Angle-only sketch of something with no right angles
instructions: Draw the angles only, on something that has no right angles anywhere.

subject.text: Something with no right angles — a plant, a shoe.

steps.name: Draw only the gaps around a chair
instructions: Draw only the gaps around the chair.
Never the chair itself.

subject.text: A chair at an oblique angle.

steps.name: Draw only the gaps between the leaves of a houseplant
instructions: Draw only the gaps between the leaves.
Never the leaves themselves.

subject.text: A monstera or spider plant.

steps.name: Draw only the gaps in a bicycle's frame and wheels
instructions: Draw only the gaps inside the frame and between the spokes.
Never the frame itself.

subject.text: A bicycle, side-on.

steps.name: Sketch, then measure against the real thing
instructions: Sketch the object.
Measure it against the real thing with a pencil at arm's length.
Note the direction of your error.

subject.text: The third item from the left on your kitchen counter.

steps.name: Two-value block-in
instructions: Block in the silhouette.
Add one internal shadow shape.

subject.text: Whatever is currently in your sink.

steps.name: Comparative proportion — two objects of different size
instructions: Draw two objects of different size.
Get their relative scale correct.
steps.commonFailure: Drawings drift too large toward the bottom of the page.

subject.text: Two things at different scales in one view — a stepladder beside a chair, or an open laptop beside a mug.

steps.name: Photo study, then a self-check pass
instructions: Draw from the photo.
Hold your drawing beside the reference.
Name the single biggest error out loud.

subject.text: A photo of one hard thing — a bicycle side-on, a staircase railing, a radiator.

steps.name: One complexity study, 30 min minimum, from life
instructions: Draw one complex subject from life.
30 minutes minimum. Stay with it.

subject.text: A kitchen sink with dishes in it, a pile of unfolded laundry, or a bookshelf corner.

whatever is currently in your sink
the corner where two walls meet the ceiling
the car parked furthest from your door, rear three-quarter
your non-drawing hand gripping a doorknob
the view out any window, but only shapes above the horizon line
